en.marketHeading: What is actually different about marketing in {city}
market: {city} has two customer bases that behave nothing alike. There are the people who live here, who search the way people search anywhere, and there are the millions of visitors who search from somewhere else entirely, days or weeks before they arrive. A campaign built for one is close to useless for the other, and the single most common problem I find in {city} accounts is one set of settings trying to serve both.

Visitor demand also means your targeting probably should not be where you are. If you sell to tourists, the useful audience is in Toronto, in Buffalo, in the GTA suburbs planning a weekend, not within a ten kilometre radius of your front door. That is an easy setting to get wrong and an expensive one to leave wrong through a whole season.

Then there is the calendar. {region}'s wine country, the falls, the theatre season and the border traffic put most of the year's demand into a handful of months. Spreading a budget evenly across twelve of them is the most reliable way to underspend in June and overspend in February, and it is the first thing I would restructure.

faq.q: Do you have an office in {city}?
faq.a: No. I am based in Toronto and work from home, so there is no {city} office and I am not going to imply there is. Everything is run remotely over video and email, which is how I run every account.

faq.q: Where should we target if our customers are visitors?
faq.a: Where the visitors are before they arrive, which for most {city} businesses means Toronto and the GTA, western New York, and the drive market beyond that. Targeting a radius around your own address is the most common and most expensive mistake in a visitor-driven account, because the people already standing outside your door are not the ones you need to reach.

faq.q: Should we advertise in the off season?
faq.a: At a much lower level, yes, and mostly to residents rather than visitors. Going completely dark means restarting from zero every spring, and the quiet months are the right time to build the SEO and the AIO presence that will be working when the season arrives.

faq.q: Which service should a {city} business start with?
faq.a: If your season is close, Google Ads with the targeting fixed first. If you are in a quiet stretch, that is the best possible time to start SEO because the work needs the runway. AIO is cheap, one time, and unusually relevant for anything a traveller would ask an assistant about.
Google Ads management is $1,500 a month plus your ad spend. SEO consulting is $1,200 a month. AIO consulting is $1,800 one time. No setup fees and no long contract.
